source.title: Signal-to-Noise Ratio and Sample Size Govern Representational Alignment in Neural Networks

record.file_problem: None noted. The text includes figure captions, but the plotted numerical values are not available in the extracted text.
record.tranche_reason: It sweeps training sample size and measures generalization error, reporting double-descent behavior in several settings; this directly tests the sample-size part of the claim.
record.gate_note: The study also reports representational-alignment results, but those measure CCE rather than test error and are not rows for these claim versions. Generalization-error results cited from prior work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps training sample size and reports test (generalization) error in linear, ReLU and CIFAR-10 CNN settings, including CIFAR-10 with label noise. This closely matches the sample-wise double-descent setup of Nakkiran et al. The generalization-error curves are secondary to the paper's alignment focus but are its own results.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but misweighted. The authors' main conclusion concerns representational alignment (CCE): it rises monotonically with SNR, varies non-monotonically with sample size with a minimum near the interpolation threshold, and is decoupled from generalization error. Double descent in generalization error and the stronger peak under label noise are reported as supporting observations, not as headline conclusions.
record.recipe_differences: Uses sample-size sweeps and generalization error, but studies its own linear, ReLU, and classification settings rather than presenting an explicit replication; it does not sweep model size or epochs.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization-error peak prominence changes with label-noise rate in the CIFAR-10 experiment. The paper also reports generalization-error behavior across different SNR values in the synthetic experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Representational alignment (CCE) between independently trained networks is minimized near the interpolation threshold, mirroring the generalization-error peak, but alignment and error are decoupled across SNR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational alignment across independently trained networks shows a sample-wise minimum at the interpolation threshold that does not track generalization error.

record.problems: The generalization-error curves and their numerical values are available only in figures in the provided text; the text gives qualitative descriptions rather than tabulated values. The CIFAR-10 label-noise rates beyond 0% are not stated here.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible generalization-error results were left out. The MNIST appendix provides a figure caption but no accompanying textual description of its generalization-error results in the supplied text.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep; CNN width is fixed at 40 feature maps in the last layer.
No epoch-wise test-error curves; representations are studied at convergence only.
No explicit statement or numbers that error increases with n over a given range; this is inferred from the double-descent shape. Tested in only these synthetic and CIFAR-10 settings.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No effective-complexity predictor of peak location across axes. Peak locations are stated only as n=d (linear) and n≈p (ReLU, CNN).
Multiple or triple descent is not tested, and neither is removal of the peak by tuned regularization. SNR dependence of peak height in the synthetic settings is not described.

missing.what: Linear vs ReLU comparison at SNR=5, k=20: the linear network's error diverges at its own threshold n/(dk)=0.05 (n=d). This is a further sample-wise peak.
MNIST FCNN generalization error vs sample size for various label noise. It is figure only; the text says only that results are qualitatively similar.

record.verdict_notes: The CIFAR-10 CNN with label noise and a sample-size sweep is close to Nakkiran et al.'s sample-wise setup, hence T1. However, the paper does not frame these results as a replication, and all generalization-error evidence is qualitative or figure-only. The linear-network double descent is also supported by an analytic formula (Eq. 33) taken from Advani et al.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures learned representations at convergence and says training dynamics are future work; it does not sweep epochs or training time for test error.
The tested sweeps vary sample size in the reported settings; other datasets, models, and training procedures are not tested.
No capacity sweep across model classes; the sweeps vary sample size.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location across size, epochs, and sample count.

The effect of label-noise rate on peak prominence is tested for CIFAR-10. The study does not test multiple or triple descent, variance as a separate cause, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameters to test whether the curve becomes an ordinary U-shape.
